expectations.text: Names the four Kirkpatrick levels: reaction, learning, behavior, results
expectations.evidence: "Level 1 — Reaction.", "Level 2 — Learning.", "Level 3 — Behavior.", "Level 4 — Results."

expectations.text: Classifies the 4.6 out of 5 rating as level 1 and the 82% quiz pass rate as level 2
expectations.evidence: "Level 1 — Reaction. ✅ You have the aggregate (4.6/5, 640 enrolled)." / "Level 2 — Learning. ✅ 82% pass rate is a healthy number"

expectations.text: Names stopping at levels 1 and 2 as the framework's own documented failure mode
expectations.evidence: The transcript describes the gap ("you have Reaction and Learning data... and zero Behavior or Results data") but never cites this as a documented, known failure mode of the Kirkpatrick framework itself.

expectations.text: States the instruction to start with Level 4, Results, attributed to Kirkpatrick Partners rather than presented as generic advice
expectations.evidence: "Design backwards from Results, per Kirkpatrick" combined with sourcing table: "Kirkpatrick's four levels and the Level 3... definition — Kirkpatrick Partners, cited as published"

expectations.text: States that levels 3 and 4 require joining learner identity to product usage
expectations.evidence: "Identity join (the actual unlock): opted-in email from the §5 certificate → your product/marketing analytics account ID → the matched-cohort comparisons above."

expectations.text: States that the identity join must be decided before launch and cannot be reconstructed after a cohort has learned anonymously
expectations.evidence: "They learned anonymously, by design, and that can't be un-done after the fact."

expectations.text: Reproduces level 3's requirement that learners be supported in and accountable for the behavior in their own environment
expectations.evidence: "behavior is 'performing critical behaviors in the environment and being supported in and accountable for that performance'"

expectations.text: Says a flat behavior metric can be an employer-support problem rather than a curriculum defect, and to check which before rewriting modules
expectations.evidence: The discussion only distinguishes prospect vs. activated-user 'environment' applicability; it never frames a flat metric as possibly an employer-support failure to check before rewriting modules.

expectations.text: Specifies exactly one primary metric per level, noting that more than one primary metric per level means none is primary
expectations.evidence: Level 4 offers "support ticket rate on covered topics, and/or usage-driven expansion" as one option, undermining single-primary-metric discipline, and no statement articulates the 'more than one means none is primary' rule.

expectations.text: Notes that Phillips adds a level 5 for ROI and that Kaufman places ROI at level 4, and instructs picking one convention and saying which
expectations.evidence: Only Phillips is mentioned ("The CFO's question sounds like it wants Phillips' Level 5 (ROI)"); Kaufman is never mentioned.

expectations.text: Refuses to claim revenue was caused by the course, and frames any link as a labelled correlation using matched comparison groups
expectations.evidence: "computing one without validated Level 4 data is inventing a number, not measuring one" combined with repeated "matched control group" framing.

expectations.text: Names opt-in selection bias: learners who enrol are already more committed, so raw before-and-after comparison overstates the effect
expectations.evidence: No discussion of selection bias from opting into the optional certificate appears anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: Names at least one level it will not measure this year and why, in advance rather than at review
expectations.evidence: "What you cannot measure this year: Behavior and Results for the 640 people already enrolled. They learned anonymously, by design..."
